subject: Close runway: short sprint interruption and mitigation register
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morales <alex.morales@cloudlytics.com>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@cloudlytics.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Close runway: short sprint interruption and mitigation register

Alex / Sara —

Thanks for the update this morning. I understand the procurement team needs an extra week to validate the data processing addendum, which impacts our previously-stated go-live target (10/01). To keep momentum, I propose a short mitigation register and a compressed sprint to protect the core delivery milestone.

Proposed immediate steps (can iterate in the MAP doc attached):
- Hold a 30-min procurement working session Monday 9/27 to align on outstanding DPA items (procurement contacts + evidence owner).
- Freeze integration cutover items that can wait (non-blocking dashboards).
- Prioritize the production performance test and a targeted acceptance test with a trimmed checklist (2 dev tickets + 1 acceptance script).
- Two-week rolling contingency: new go/no-go checkpoint on 10/08.

I attached a one-page MAP snapshot (MAP-v3.pdf) and a procurement snapshot we pulled together. If this works, I’ll share an updated MAP with dates and owners. We want to avoid stretching the timeline further while giving procurement the time they need.

Can you confirm who from your procurement team will attend Monday?

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-v3.pdf (1 page summary), procurement-snapshot-2027-09-24.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Alex Morales <alex.morales@cloudlytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@cloudlytics.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 12:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Close runway: short sprint interruption and mitigation register

Kimberly —

Appreciate the quick plan. Procurement will need the DPA clarifications signed off by their legal lead; I’ve looped Sara to coordinate. We can do Monday 9/27 at 10am PT — I’ll invite Michael Cho (procurement lead) and Liza Park (legal counsel).

Two notes from our side:
1) The procurement hold is primarily around the retention and logging clauses; legal is also asking for runbook details for incident triage.
2) Our internal PM is flagging that moving the acceptance window to 10/08 will still be tight if we lose more than one day of integration work.

We’ll join Monday and come with questions. If you can send a slim MAP with owners before the call that’d be helpful.

— Alex
VP Product, CloudLytics
alex.morales@cloudlytics.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Morales <alex.morales@cloudlytics.com>, Sara Lin <sara.lin@cloudlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Close runway: short sprint interruption and mitigation register

Kim / Aditya —

Looping in our CS playbook and risk coverage notes before the Monday session. Quick internal read:
- Risk severity: medium-high (procurement hold + logging evidence ask).
- Operational exposure: if legal requests >3 rounds of redline, we should expect another 7–10 business days.

Immediate internal asks for the Monday meeting:
- Kimberly: bring the reduced-scope acceptance checklist (one-pager).
- Aditya: can you confirm whether we can offer a limited runbook excerpt (non-prod incident triage) as evidence to procurement? If we can, that often short-circuits objections.
- I’ll prepare an expedited rollback and contingency note for shared visibility.

If we anticipate >1 week slippage, we should prepare an executive note (brief) offering a small startup credit to preserve goodwill and keep the contractual timelines tractable.

— Laura
Customer Success Director, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

On Mon, Sep 27, 2027 at 07:55 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick confirmation: Monday 10am PT works for CloudLytics procurement. I’ll share the trimmed acceptance checklist before the call.
From: Alex Morales <alex.morales@cloudlytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@cloudlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Close runway: short sprint interruption and mitigation register

Thanks all — the call today was useful. Quick outcomes to capture on the thread so the MAP remains current:
- Procurement will accept a non-prod incident triage runbook excerpt and clarified retention schedule; legal to provide redline by EOD Wed (9/29).
- CloudLytics will complete the remaining integration ticket that blocks production test by Thu (9/30).
- New go/no-go checkpoint moved to Fri 10/08, with acceptance window 10/11–10/15 if all criteria pass.

We expect legal’s redline to be light, but if they come back with additional requirements we’ll escalate.

Alex

On Mon, Sep 27, 2027 at 10:01 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai> wrote:

Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Close runway: short sprint interruption and mitigation register — exec alignment

Team —

Thanks for the summary, Alex. I’ve reviewed the MAP snapshot and the contingency plan. Two quick decisions from leadership to avoid downstream churn:
1) We’ll provision a targeted technical runbook excerpt and an incident triage summary for procurement (non-prod) by EOD Wed 9/29. Laura — please own the artifact and I’ll help with clearance.
2) Approve a one-time $4,000 implementation credit if legal’s final redline requires a change that materially delays launch beyond 10/08. The credit is conditional on CloudLytics completing the integration ticket by 9/30 and continuing to meet the acceptance checklist.

I’ll draft a short executive note to Alex summarizing these commitments and will post to HubSpot.

-Aditya
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
